source.title: Questions for Flat-Minima Optimization of Modern Neural Networks
source.authors: Jean Kaddour; Linqing Liu; Ricardo M. A. Silva; Matt J. Kusner

record.tranche_reason: The study measures Hessian curvature and evaluates held-out performance across optimizers, examining whether flatness relates to generalization. It does not use the magnitude-aware sharpness measure specified in V7.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own curvature and test-performance results. The broad benchmark results do not report training error alongside test error for each optimizer; cited findings from other papers were excluded.
record.test_reason: Appendix A.6 directly compares SGD with momentum and AdamW on ResNet-34/CIFAR-100: test accuracy is 76.14% versus 72.14%. This bears on V4 under a restricted protocol that switches optimizers while holding the learning rate and other hyperparameters fixed. The Hessian analysis does not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that SWA/SAM effectiveness depends on task and architecture, averaging SAM iterates often improves performance, and failure cases can exhibit misalignment between training and test loss minimizers.
record.recipe_differences: Compares SWA, SAM, and averaged SAM iterates across tasks; measures dominant Hessian eigenvalues and evaluates generalization rather than magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that optimizer effectiveness varies by dataset and architecture; the base optimizer and data augmentation also change outcomes in the reported ablations.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports lower dominant Hessian eigenvalues for SAM than SWA in both analyzed tasks, with WASAM lowest: 117 on WRN/CIFAR-100 and 9.96 on GIN/Code2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM and weight averaging can reduce unscaled local Hessian curvature in these two settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the benchmark, SWA and SAM have task- and architecture-dependent held-out benefits; the GraphSAGE/Proteins failure analysis finds misaligned training and test loss minimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Flat-minima optimization methods do not uniformly improve held-out performance, and training-loss geometry can misalign with test performance.

record.problems: The curvature-to-generalization evidence is limited to two tasks in the flatness analysis; the Hessian values do not directly measure training-to-test gaps. The authors note that some shared hyperparameters may harm flat-optimizer results and that fully independent tuning was infeasible.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many optimizer-versus-baseline benchmark results in Tables 2 and 4 and Figures 4–5, but these do not test any listed version or provide the training-to-test-gap measure specified by the claim. Interpolation figures are not converted to numeric rows.

untested.parts: Matched random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected training from scratch and the contribution of local connectivity.

Separately tuned learning rates and schedules, broader tuning that could remove the difference, matched training performance, switching optimizers during training, and language-model comparisons. The optimizer-switch ablation uses one seed per image-classification condition.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted large-batch recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with training-to-test error gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized examples versus matched random removal.

missing.what: Add the direct ResNet-34/CIFAR-100 baseline optimizer comparison: momentum SGD test accuracy 76.14%, AdamW 72.14%, with all other hyperparameters held fixed and one random seed each. Although Table 4 is declared in rows_left_out, its exclusion as irrelevant is incorrect; it supplies the study's V4 evidence.
missing.locator: Appendix A.6, Table 4, baseline column and accompanying discussion

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly marks V4 untested. Its Table 4 ablation supports an optimizer difference under fixed shared settings, but cannot establish performance after fair independent tuning. Neither induced flatness nor raw Hessian eigenvalues directly tests V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under differing tuning protocols.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its ranking against norm and margin measures, and correlations across a convolutional family trained to similarly low loss.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: ResNet-34 on CIFAR-100; AdamW versus momentum SGD with shared hyperparameters held fixed; one seed each.
relationships.reason: Appendix A.6/Table 4 reports 72.14% test accuracy for AdamW versus 76.14% for SGD, a 4.00-point deficit. The authors also report AdamW underfitting. Verdict rests on text because R1–R8 omit this comparison.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower AdamW accuracy than momentum SGD and accompanying underfitting remain unverified, with one seed per optimizer.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
